q: Which correctly matches each stage of aerobic respiration to its location in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Glycolysis: matrix · Krebs cycle: cytoplasm · Electron transport chain: outer membrane
Glycolysis: intermembrane space · Krebs cycle: cristae · Electron transport chain: mitochondrial matrix
Glycolysis: cytoplasm · Link reaction & Krebs: matrix · Electron transport chain: inner membrane
All stages take place in the matrix, where every respiratory enzyme is dissolved
explanation: Glycolysis enzymes are in the cytoplasm; pyruvate is then transported into the matrix, which holds the link-reaction and Krebs enzymes. Electron carriers and ATP synthase are embedded in the inner membrane (folded into cristae), which separates the matrix from the narrow intermembrane space where H+ accumulates. Compartments let each stage have its own enzymes and conditions.
